test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 16 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.**

Although Shagun was competently doing the project on her own, Pranav couldn't stop himself from (giving her unnecessary advice).
solution:
The correct answer is: **Being a backseat driver**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**being a backseat driver**" means to give unwanted advice or to criticize someone who is already doing something well. (अवांछित सलाह देना या किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति की आलोचना करना जो पहले से ही कुछ अच्छा कर रहा है)
 
• The phrase comes from the idea of someone sitting in the backseat of a car and telling the driver what to do, even though they are not actually driving.
 
• In the given sentence, Pranav is interfering with Shagun's work by giving her unnecessary advice, hence the idiom "being a backseat driver" fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Devil's advocate**: This phrase means to argue against something, even if you don't believe in it, in order to test its strength or validity. (किसी चीज़ के ख़िलाफ़ बहस करना, भले ही आप उस पर विश्वास न करें, ताकि उसकी ताकत या वैधता का परीक्षण किया जा सके)
 
• **A bitter pill to swallow**: This idiom means to accept something unpleasant or difficult. (किसी अप्रिय या कठिन बात को स्वीकार करना)
 
• **Cutting the mustard**: This idiom means to meet expectations or to perform satisfactorily. (अपेक्षाओं पर खरा उतरना या संतोषजनक प्रदर्शन करना)
